svg.aria-label: NISAR's 24 cm radar wave passes through the forest canopy and returns from the peat surface; if the ground sinks 2 cm between passes 12 days apart, the echo comes back 60 degrees later in its cycle
svg.text: How NISAR measures the ground under a forest
NISAR's L-band radar has a 24 cm wavelength, long enough to pass through the canopy and come back from the peat.
so most of the wave passes.
NISAR images the same spot again 12 days later. The ground has
sunk 2 cm in between, so the echo arrives later in its cycle.
The echo's round trip grows by
As a share of the wavelength
So the echo's phase shifts by
A full 360° cycle corresponds to 12 cm.
Each location is compared across many passes. Because the phase repeats every 12 cm, larger movements are tracked across neighbouring pixels and over time.
